answer: Give voting weight only for unbroken tenure: an identity earns weight slowly, one epoch at a time, while it stays active and honest. Weight is non-transferable and resets to zero if the identity changes hands or goes quiet. A farmer can mint a grove of ten thousand names overnight, but cannot fast-forward their seniority — each clone must sit through the same slow seasons, like yarrow spreading one root at a time. Buying old identities fails too, since a transfer wipes the velvet record clean. Limit: newcomers start weak, so tenure caps at a modest ceiling to keep fresh voices audible.
